name: Cradle Mountain
reason: Iconic summit named by Wikivoyage, Discover Tasmania; day walk from Dove Lake.

name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
reason: Flagship World Heritage park, Wikivoyage, Parks Tasmania, Discover Tasmania.

name: Dove Lake
reason: Glacial lake under Cradle Mountain with the 6 km loop track; named by Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania.

name: Lake St Clair
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania: Australia's deepest lake, visitor centre at Cynthia Bay, ferry and walks.

name: Overland Track
reason: Australia's most famous multi-day walk, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania; fee/booking system, season.

name: Dove Lake Loop Track
reason: Part of Dove Lake: a shoreline loop of the lake the app lists (rule 3).

name: Marion's Lookout
reason: Named Wikivoyage day walk (2 h return) to a Dove Lake viewpoint; a distinct half-day outing (rules 1-2).

name: Hanson's Peak
reason: Named 2 h Wikivoyage walk with Cradle/Dove Lake views; single source.

name: Barn Bluff
reason: Named Wikivoyage mountain climb off the Overland Track; real but 10 h and for experienced walkers.

name: Cathedral Mountain
reason: Peak seen from the Overland Track; no specific visitor outing in the source (rule 2).

name: Mount Ossa
reason: Tasmania's highest peak, climbed via Pelion Gap; a named Wikivoyage objective with high public interest.

name: Pencil Pine Falls
reason: Short boardwalk rainforest walk behind the visitor centre; Wikivoyage calls it a must for all visitors.

name: Enchanted Walk
reason: Half-hour dry walk past waterfalls and rainforest, named by Wikivoyage.

name: Weindorfers Forest Walk
reason: 20-minute loop from Waldheim; part of the Waldheim stop (rule 3).

name: Waldheim Chalet
reason: Gustav Weindorfer's 1912 chalet with displays; a heritage site visitors can enter, named by the guide (rules 1-2).

name: Waterfall Valley
reason: Hut and campsite stop on the Overland Track, no sight of its own (rule 2/3).

name: Lake Rodway
reason: Alpine lake with Scott-Kilvert Hut, 6 h return walk; Wikivoyage-named.

name: Kitchen Hut
reason: Day-use hut on the Marion's Lookout route; part of that walk (rule 3).

name: Cradle Mountain Summit Walk
reason: The headline day walk to the summit of Cradle Mountain from Dove Lake; Wikivoyage names it (rule 1).

name: Lake Barrington
reason: Trout lake, rafting and lakeside walks near Sheffield; the Discover Tasmania page was opened but did not clearly list it.

name: Mount Roland
reason: Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania: peak with 360-degree summit walk above Sheffield.

name: Dial Range
reason: Coastal walks with views over Penguin, Wikivoyage 'Do' entry.

name: Devils Gullet
reason: Named lookout platform over a sheer cliff with views to Cradle Mountain, near Mole Creek (rules 1-2).

name: Great Western Tiers
reason: A broad escarpment/range of many walks, not one place (rule 3).

name: Leven Canyon
reason: Two Wikivoyage pages name it: a 275 m lookout reached on a short walk (rules 1-2).

name: Hellyer Gorge
reason: Walking tracks along the Hellyer River, named by Wikivoyage.

name: Gunns Plains Caves
reason: Show cave (guided tours) named by Wikivoyage Ulverstone/Penguin chain and tourism sources; a real half-hour+ visit.

name: King Solomon's Cave
reason: Show cave in the Mole Creek Karst, listed by Wikivoyage (rules 1-2).

name: Marakoopa Cave
reason: Glow-worm show cave in Mole Creek Karst, listed by Wikivoyage; a distinct tour.

name: Mole Creek Karst National Park
reason: Only Tasmanian park protecting caves (Marakoopa and King Solomons guided tours); Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania.

name: Walls of Jerusalem National Park
reason: World Heritage park with multi-day and day walks, Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania.

name: Walls of Jerusalem Multi-Day Walk
reason: Promoted multi-day loop in the national park (benchmark: Hump Ridge Track).

name: The Temple
reason: A summit side trip inside the Walls of Jerusalem walk (rule 3).

name: Solomons Throne
reason: A rock feature inside the Walls of Jerusalem walk (rule 3).

name: Pool of Bethesda
reason: Wikipedia article and 96143 views and coordinates (31.78, 35.24) are for the biblical pool in Jerusalem, not the Tasmanian tarn; the real tarn is only a passing mention in Wikivoyage's park page, part of the Walls of Jerusalem walk.

name: King David's Peak
reason: A peak climbed within the Walls of Jerusalem trip (rule 3).

name: Stanley
reason: Historic fishing village with visitor centre, Highfield Historic Site, penguin viewing and the Nut; Wikivoyage page.

name: The Nut
reason: Volcanic plug with chairlift and 4.6 km summit circuit, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania.

name: Highfield Historic Site
reason: Colonial homestead open daily with self-guided tours; Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania both name it.

name: Little Penguin Viewing Area Stanley
reason: Free dusk viewing of fairy penguins at Stanley, a wildlife encounter named by Wikivoyage.

name: Trethewies Lookout
reason: Roadside pull-out photo stop with no named walk (rule 3).

name: Godfreys Beach
reason: Second-tier beach at Stanley with views of The Nut, named by Wikivoyage.

name: Edge of the World
reason: Wikivoyage names it as the signature stop on the west coast; coastal cliffs/viewpoint, free, always open.

name: Sandy Cape Beach
reason: Largest beach in the Arthur-Pieman but reached by a 48 km return track needing a driver pass.

name: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania name it; wild beaches, Sandy Cape Track and visitor centre (rule 1-2).

name: Takayna / Tarkine
reason: Named by Discover Tasmania as a wilderness region of rainforest and coast; a region, not one place.

name: Balfour
reason: Ghost town stop on the Tarkine drive per Wikivoyage.

name: Greens Beach
reason: Surf beach, but the listing says it is at Marrawah (1 h 45 west of Burnie) while a Greens Beach also lies near Narawntapu; the target must be resolved first.

name: Narawntapu National Park
reason: National park with Wikivoyage entry and Parks Tasmania; wildlife (wombats, wallabies) and beaches.

name: Bakers Beach
reason: Longest beach in Narawntapu National Park with sunset views; named by Wikivoyage.

name: Badger Beach Lookout
reason: Minor lookout within Narawntapu National Park (rule 3).

name: Rocky Cape National Park
reason: Parks Tasmania, Wikivoyage; coastal walks, caves and lighthouse-style headland views.

name: Rocky Cape Lighthouse
reason: 1968 lighthouse, one of the park's main points of interest per Wikivoyage.

name: North Cave
reason: Short walk to an Aboriginal shelter cave in Rocky Cape National Park; a cultural sight.

name: Sisters Beach
reason: Beach near Wynyard named by two Wikivoyage pages with walks to Anniversary Bay and Rocky Cape.

name: Boat Harbour Beach
reason: Wikivoyage names the turquoise little bay as a stop; second-tier beach, always there.

name: Somerset Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Burnie and Western Tasmania: swimming beach along Somerset coast, but the pin is the Somerset town centre point.

name: Fossil Bluff
reason: Beach with layered rock and fossils plus a short lookout walk; Wikivoyage Wynyard see entry (2.6k views).

name: Table Cape
reason: Wikivoyage Wynyard and Western Tasmania: headland lookout and lighthouse; free.

name: Wonders of Wynyard
reason: Exhibition centre on local history with posted opening hours, Wikivoyage.

name: Burnie Regional Museum
reason: Museum with a Federation Street recreated streetscape; Wikivoyage.

name: Little Penguin Observation Centre
reason: Free guided penguin viewing at sunset Oct-Mar at Parsonage Point, Burnie (Wikivoyage).

name: Fernglade
reason: Fern reserve on the Emu River with a chance of platypus; Wikivoyage.

name: Guide Falls
reason: Waterfall in a picnic reserve south of Burnie, named by Wikivoyage; a second-tier natural stop.

name: Emu Valley Rhododendron Garden
reason: 13-hectare garden open daily with hours listed by Wikivoyage (rules 1-2).

name: Devonport
reason: Gateway city with its own Wikivoyage chapter: Mersey Bluff lighthouse and penguin viewing, Tiagarra cultural centre, Don River Railway (rule 1-2).

name: Mersey Bluff Lighthouse
reason: Devonport headland lighthouse and evening penguin-viewing area listed by Wikivoyage with coordinates; the bluff is the stop.

name: Bass Strait Maritime Centre
reason: Daily maritime museum on Bass Strait history in Devonport (Wikivoyage).

name: Don River Railway
reason: Vintage steam railway and pioneer village at Don; a heritage rail with a base station and museum, not a vehicle only.

name: Tiagarra Aboriginal Culture Centre
reason: Aboriginal museum with a nature trail to rock formations at Mersey Bluff (Wikivoyage).

name: Tasmanian Arboretum
reason: 66 ha arboretum open 9am to sunset with platypus and water birds (Wikivoyage).

name: Back Beach
reason: Devonport's main beach, listed in See.

name: Ulverstone
reason: Wikivoyage page lists only cafes, a volunteer-run history museum and surrounding sites (Lillico Beach, Leven Canyon); the town has no own draw.

name: Lillico Beach
reason: Beach where little penguins walk up the sand each evening (Wikivoyage).

name: Ulverstone History Museum
reason: Volunteer-run local history museum open a few afternoon hours (rule 2).

name: Kaydale Lodge Gardens
reason: 3 ha garden at Nietta with teas, named by Wikivoyage.

name: Penguin
reason: Seaside town with the Big Penguin icon, heritage trail and beach; Wikivoyage lists it only as 'home of the Big Penguin', no town page.

name: Big Penguin
reason: Giant penguin sculpture, a quirky roadside icon named by Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania (benchmark: Ohakune Carrot).

name: Penguin General Cemetery and Vantage Point
reason: Heritage cemetery doubling as a free 24-hour lookout.

name: Penguin Heritage Trail
reason: A walking route linking existing town sights, not a distinct place (rule 3).

name: Sheffield
reason: Town of Murals: permanent large murals, named by Wikivoyage Western Tasmania and Discover Tasmania; the town itself is the draw (rule 3).

name: Deloraine
reason: Gateway town and regional hub for Cradle, Mole Creek and the Highland Lakes with its own Wikivoyage page.

name: Big Coffee Pot
reason: Giant coffee pot silo, a quirky roadside icon listed by Wikivoyage Deloraine.

name: Mole Creek
reason: Town beside Mole Creek Karst, the caves' base; two Wikivoyage pages.

name: Latrobe
reason: Historic town with Gilbert Street heritage, Axemans Hall of Fame and platypus viewing; only one real-sourced listing (Wikivoyage Latrobe (Tasmania) page); town itself is a modest draw.

name: Australian Axeman's Hall of Fame
reason: Quirky museum of wood-chopping in Latrobe, open daily (Wikivoyage).

name: Latrobe Court House Museum
reason: Small local-history museum run by the National Trust (rule 2/3).

name: Smithton
reason: Dairy town and base for the Circular Head area per Wikivoyage.

name: Allendale Gardens and Rainforest Walks
reason: Gardens and rainforest walks near Smithton, weekdays in season.

name: Somerset
reason: Small coastal town with a beach; no sight of its own named by the guide.

name: Arthur River
reason: Gateway village for the Tarkine / Edge of the World drive; draws are beyond it (benchmark: Pipiriki).

name: Beaconsfield
reason: Town wrapper beside its own attraction, Beaconsfield Mine and Heritage Centre (WIKI: town only a spot when the town is itself a draw).

name: Beaconsfield Mine and Heritage Centre
reason: Heritage centre at the mine site on gold-mining and the 2006 collapse, open daily (Wikivoyage).
